questions.prompt: Which question defines the service model's intended boundary in Chapter 3?

options.text: How many devices does the library own?
Can a front-desk worker make a correct room decision while the live view is unavailable?
Which vendor has the most features?
Was any contact-list record ever exported?

questions.explanation: The model includes parts needed for the bounded booking decision, not every device or an unrelated announcement workflow.

questions.prompt: Which classification matches the small proposed model?

options.text: Resident is a store; reservation store is a person
Printed schedule is the authoritative live process
Booking view is a process; reservation store is a data store; printed schedule is a copy
Event contacts are the booking request flow

questions.explanation: The chapter distinguishes people or external entities, processes, retained stores and physical copies without claiming verified architecture.

questions.prompt: Why is the event-contact list excluded from the traced booking-decision path?

options.text: It has no security needs
It serves announcements, not the particular room decision being modeled
Its records have been verified as public
Staff automatically may export it

questions.explanation: The narrow decision boundary excludes a different-purpose data set without claiming that it is safe or unimportant.

questions.prompt: At 11:42, what does the fixed 09:00 printout prove about SYN-002 created at 10:05?

options.text: It cannot include that later booking under the stated snapshot assumption
It proves Room 2 at 15:00 is free
It proves the store lost SYN-002
It proves a resident received a confirmation

questions.explanation: A fixed copy predates SYN-002. Its silence cannot establish current availability or the state of a real reservation store.

questions.prompt: What is the pending request queue in the tabletop model?

options.text: A record of unverified requests that still needs reconciliation
An authoritative confirmed booking
A replacement for all reservation records
Proof of the outage's cause

questions.explanation: The queue records a provisional front-desk decision but is not a current booking source or confirmation.

questions.prompt: What does crossing the resident-to-booking-view trust boundary show by itself?

options.text: Authentication and authorization are implemented correctly
Encryption is absent
Every resident can edit staff reservations
A change of authority worth checking; no control implementation is proved

questions.explanation: A boundary points to a verification question. The proposed arrow is not evidence that a particular safeguard exists or works.

questions.prompt: Which sentence describes a conditional dependency rather than a data flow?

options.text: A booking request moves from resident to booking view
The diagram proves one physical database
If the reservation store is unavailable, saving a booking may fail absent an approved fallback
A printout has a timestamp

questions.explanation: A dependency states what an outcome requires under a condition; a flow describes proposed movement of information.

questions.prompt: A hypothetical messaging supplier delays confirmation. What can the model conclude about saving the reservation?

options.text: The reservation definitely failed
The reservation definitely succeeded
Delivery and saving are separate outcomes; the owner must confirm whether they are coupled
The messaging supplier is confirmed to exist

questions.explanation: A delayed message alone does not establish persistence. The supplier and coupling are unverified teaching possibilities.

questions.prompt: An owner reports an approved 11:40 offline sheet with SYN-002, but nobody has checked it. What changes?

options.text: The old 09:00 sheet is now known to be current
All previous observations must be erased
Room 2 can be promised immediately
The report weakens the stale-only assumption, pending a safe timestamp and content check

questions.explanation: The new report is relevant evidence to examine, not an independently verified sheet; decisions branch on its approved status and check.

questions.prompt: The model does not mention a recovery mechanism. Which conclusion is justified?

options.text: No recovery exists
The service has a single point of failure
The printed schedule is a tested recovery system
Recovery remains an open question for the owner, not evidence of absence

questions.explanation: A missing description cannot prove absence. The model must label uncertainty and seek owner-confirmed facts.
